description: An adult herring gull standing in a closed horizontal wedge, its folded wings tucked inside the body outline with crossed near-black primaries projecting a hand's width past a tapered tail, a short blunt hooked bill, a heavy convex belly and scaled webbed feet with dark curled claws; the head, throat, breast, belly and tail are a pale cool sea-foam grey, the mantle and folded wing coverts a flat weathered zinc grey the colour of galvanised rail, the outer wingtips deep storm black, the bill a dull unpolished brass tone with a small oxide-red spot on the lower mandible and a thin oxide-red ring around a pale blank clay-grey iris, and the legs and webs a muted desaturated clay-pink; patchy dried salt crust whitens the crown and upper mantle, the shoulders and back are rain-soaked into separated wet feather spikes while the breast stays dry and lofted, one outer primary on the left wing is broken short, and a faint grey oil film smears the lower breast.
dimensions: 0.62 m from bill tip to tail tip, 1.44 m wingspan, 0.38 m tall standing
negative: No pure white, cream or ivory plumage, no yellow bill, no bright pink or scarlet legs, no metallic or polished sheen anywhere, no spread, raised or heraldic wings, no second bird or flock, no perch, rail, rock or ground plane, no rivets, chamfers, flanges or machined edges, no injury, blood or missing eye, no text, no watermark and no human figures.
